question:
Match Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana Categories with the Loan Amount as updated in the Union Budget 2023-24 and select the correct answer.

 
 

 
 
**List I**

 
**(Mudra Loans Categories)**

 
 
 
**List II**

 
**(Loan Amount)**

 
 
 

 
 
1.

 
 Shishu
 
 
A.

 
 Upto ₹50,000
 
 

 
 
2.

 
 Kishor
 
 
B.

 
 Above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh
 
 

 
 
3.

 
 Tarun 
 
 
C.

 
 Above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh 
 
 

 
 
4.

 
 Tarun Plus
 
 
D.

 
 Above ₹10 lakh and up to ₹20 lakh

solution:
The correct answer is __**1 - A, 2 - B, 3 - C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) offers loans under three categories: Shishu, Kishor, and Tarun.
 
• Shishu category loans are provided for amounts up to ₹50,000.
 
• Kishor category loans cover amounts above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh.
 
• Tarun category loans are for amounts above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh.
 
• The scheme aims to support small businesses, entrepreneurs, and startups by providing necessary financial assistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)**:

 
 
• Launched by the Government of India in April 2015.
 
• Aimed at providing financial support to micro and small enterprises.
 
• MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd.
 
• The scheme provides refinance support to banks and microfinance institutions.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria**:
 
 
• Any Indian citizen who has a business plan for a non-farm income-generating activity.
 
• Activities such as manufacturing, processing, trading, or service sector activities.
 
• Loan can be availed through any of the participating banks, financial institutions, or microfinance institutions.
 
 
 
• **Implementation**:
 
 
• The scheme is implemented through Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) including Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, State Cooperative Banks, Urban Cooperative Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), and Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs).
 
 
 
• **Impact**:
 
 
• The scheme has significantly contributed to job creation and the growth of the micro-enterprise sector in India.
 
• It has enabled financial inclusion by providing access to credit to the underserved and unserved population.
